children: Wonder, a food delivery startup led by former Walmart executive Marc Lore, is exploring a sale of Grubhub, The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.
and other retailers about a potential acquisition, the report added.

Wonder acquired Grubhub in 2024 for $650 million, including $500 million of senior notes and $150 million in cash. The price was a fraction of the $7.3 billion that European meal delivery group Just Eat Takeaway paid for the business in 2020 during the pandemic-driven boom in food delivery.
A potential sale would come amid broader consolidation in the food and grocery delivery industry.

Rival DoorDash agreed in October to acquire Instacart in a $17 billion deal to strengthen its position in the fast-growing U.S. grocery delivery market as competition among app-based delivery platforms intensifies.
Earlier this year, Grubhub sold its college-campus food delivery business to DoorDash for $300 million. DoorDash also invested $125 million in Wonder as part of the transaction.
There are no guarantees a deal will come together, The Wall Street Journal said, citing the people.
Target declined to comment. Wonder, Walmart and Kroger did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.
